answer: Sybil desks flood juries with cheap rater names. An applicant books haven stall HV-22, delivers a 12.4 ml sealed nectar vial (lot NV-4417, 17.6 °Brix) inside copper ampoule CA-29, and locks 21,300 tokens for 4.5 hours before any vote counts. Clerks weigh the ampoule at minutes 11 and 39; mass must stay 91.8±0.2 g, the 11-character etch must match the posted hash, and Brix must hold within 0.3. A reused etch, diluted vial, or 0.3 g drift slashes 52% of the bond and bars the alias for 13 epochs. Forty copies lock 852,000 tokens and risk 443,040 on one failed weigh; one ampoule cannot be shared.
